Suddenly, I regain consciousness. I feel distraught, confused, my senses distorted. My vision begins to adjust to the light of a hot, mid-summer day. I find myself face up, gazing at a bright blue sky, clear and unmoving. It's just a brilliant canopy, seemingly infinite in its depth. I lie flat on my back, the feeling of soft sand below me. Unfamiliar yet warm, strange yet comforting. I hear the crashing of waves from an unknown ocean that plays in front of me, the smell of salt and brine stings my nose. I lift my head to see the ocean in all its cerulean glory, it's breathtaking. It seems like it goes on forever. There are a plethora of tropical fish bursting from the ocean, large pockets of energetic motion teeming with life. Though I see no signs of distant islands, no signs of humankind. I then look down at myself, I'm wearing a ragged blue t-shirt covered in holes, stained with sweat, and a pair of discolored brown cargo pants covered in sand. I look to my left. There are two additional tattered shirts. One solid white, one solid black, and a pile of shredded cloth that was at one point an article of clothing. They appear to have been blue jeans. I then look to my right. There is a hunting knife. It's dull, presumably worn down by both time and usage. Beside that lies a rusted metal bowl with 7 old, waterlogged matches resting within. Suddenly, I feel a sharp pain in my stomach, a sickness washes over me. I realize I'm starving. I slowly bring my hands up to my face, I feel gaunt, my face is cold despite the scorching mid-summer sun beating down on me. I begin to feel my whole body ache, a feeling of total weakness overwhelms me. I moan in agony as I lift up my ragged shirt, I can see my ribcage, there is no muscle, there is no fat, there is nothing. It's thinly covered by my sickly, grey skin. As I begin to realize the gravity of my situation, I panic. "What is happening, how did I get here, what the fuck is going on?". The thoughts race through my mind violently, I grasp for any explanation to my current condition. My mind begins to deteriorate my thoughts become more disorganized and slow. With the last of my willpower and stamina, in a dry and raspy voice I yell, "Help me, please, anyone. Please help me." My cries project outwards, only to be quickly drowned out by crashing waves of an unknown ocean. I'm alone. Hopelessly alone. A single tear rolls down my gaunt, grey cheek. I realize the end is upon me. I give that brilliant, infinite, seemingly everlasting canopy one last glance. Slowly, I close my eyes and let the waves crash and play.
